summary: Written statement of 17 November 2025 opened consultation on the first legally binding national PM2.5 targets under the Environment (Air Quality and Soundscapes) (Wales) Act 2024: an annual mean of 10 micrograms per cubic metre and a 25 percent cut in average population exposure against a 2017 to 2019 baseline, both by the end of 2035. The consultation closed on 16 February 2026. The Welsh Government published its summary of responses and government response in August 2026 (page updated 25 August): 42 responses showed broad support, some wanting the targets sooner or tougher, and the government said it will proceed with the regulations as originally drafted, adding a non-statutory aspiration to reach 10 micrograms by 2030 where feasible. The 2024 Act requires the draft PM2.5 target regulations to be laid within three years of its Royal Assent on 14 February 2024, so by 14 February 2027; they had not been laid by 6 October 2026.
title: Draft Air Quality Target Regulations for fine particulate matter (PM2.5) under the 2024 Act
